standard.title: Plan, create and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations for audiences and purposes, selecting language features, literary devices, visual features and features of voice to suit formal or informal situations, and organising and developing ideas in texts in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations for audiences and purposes, selecting features of voice and language (AC9E7LY07). They have not yet focused on the full planning-rehearsal-delivery cycle with deliberate selection of literary devices and visual features, or on calibrating voice features for specific audience effects.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations with deliberate selection of language, literary, visual and voice features for specific purposes and audiences.

nodes.label: Planning and crafting presentations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a spoken or multimodal presentation that makes deliberate selections of language features, literary devices, visual features and voice features, organising and developing ideas for a specific purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plan for a spoken or multimodal presentation that identifies at least two feature selections (e.g. tone, vocabulary, a simile, visual support) and explains how each will serve the purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Plan spoken and multimodal presentations for a range of purposes and audiences; select vocabulary, sentence structures, literary devices and features of voice with deliberate attention to purpose and audience; integrate multimodal features (visual, audio, structural) to support understanding.
wider: Plan a persuasive advertising campaign about a contemporary issue, making explicit decisions about visual design, language choices and voice features for a target audience
Compare how the same ideas require different planning and feature selection choices when delivered as a formal speech vs an informal talk vs a debate speech

Investigate how First Nations Australian oral presentation traditions (e.g. Welcome to Country, formal public speaking) use voice features and structural conventions that differ from Western formal speech conventions

response_modes.reason: Planning a presentation with deliberate voice, language and visual feature selections requires students to think ahead about audience effect — an intentional design move rather than reactive drafting. Without explicit scaffolding of what presentation planning involves (feature choices, audience considerations, structural decisions), students produce a content outline rather than a delivery plan.

success_criteria: Produces a presentation plan that identifies specific feature selections and explains their purpose.
Can justify why chosen features suit the presentation's purpose and intended audience.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 is rehearsal and delivery — a phase entirely dependent on what was planned and crafted at Node 1. Students with thin planning arrive at rehearsal without deliberate feature choices to practise or multimodal elements to integrate. Delivery becomes improvised rather than purposeful.

nodes.label: Rehearsing and delivering for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can rehearse and deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation, using features of voice — tone, volume, pitch, pace — with attention to the effects these have on audience reaction and acceptance of ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a spoken presentation and demonstrate deliberate use of at least one voice feature (tone, volume, pitch or pace) for an intended audience effect.
nodes.typical_width: Rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations, selecting and using features of voice with attention to their effect on audience response; integrate multimodal features in a presentation to support audience understanding; reflect on the effectiveness of delivery choices.
wider: Deliver a debate speech that uses voice features and vocabulary deliberately to persuade an audience and evaluate own performance against intended effect
Create a voiceover for a media presentation, selecting voice features that complement visual elements to construct a persuasive or informative effect
Reflect systematically on own presentation delivery — using video self-review or peer feedback — and identify specific voice feature improvements to rehearse

response_modes.reason: Confident, controlled presentation delivery is a fluency skill. Understanding which voice features to use does not automatically translate into being able to deploy them under the pressure of performance. Multiple rehearsal and delivery opportunities — in low-stakes and then higher-stakes contexts — build the composure and control the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Debate, formal speech, voiceover and media presentation each require qualitatively different deployment of voice features and multimodal integration. For advancing students, the diversity of presentation contexts — including preparation for formal competitive or public contexts — offers rich and motivating extended practice.
success_criteria: Delivers a presentation that demonstrates deliberate use of at least one voice feature (tone, volume, pitch or pace).
Can reflect on the intended and actual effect of voice feature choices on the audience.
